summary: Owned agents; active by default. Optional status/search. Stable created_at DESC, agent_id DESC ordering. Bare array. Strict bounds: invalid queries return 400 invalid_agent_list.
notes:
Returns a bare array of your agents; active only unless status is supplied.
Each item has the same safe settings projection as create/update/get.
Disabled agents can be listed with status=disabled or status=all, or fetched by owned ID.
Carrier auth tokens and unreviewed future columns are never returned.

| Parameter | Contract |
|---|---|
| limit | Integer 1..200, default 100 |
| offset | Integer 0..1000000, default 0 |
| status | active (default), disabled, all |
| search | Case-insensitive literal substring of name or agent_id; up to 200 characters, no control characters; leading/trailing whitespace trimmed; empty = no search |

Numbers must be decimal digits without signs, leading zeros (except 0), fractions,
exponents or trailing text. Repeated/array/object values are rejected.
Invalid query values return `400 invalid_agent_list`, not silent clamping/defaults.
Use the documented bounds and encode query values.

Order is `created_at DESC, agent_id DESC`, including tied creation times. Pages are
not a snapshot: concurrent creation, enabling/disabling or edits may shift offsets.
Every filter remains scoped to the authenticated API key. Search cannot change that.
Special characters such as %, _, *, quotes and parentheses are literal, not wildcards.

Example: `GET /v1/agents?status=all&search=Support&limit=50&offset=50`.
URL-encode search values (the kits do this automatically).

Node: `client.agents.list({status:'all',search:'Support',limit:50,offset:50})`.
`client.agents.iter(200)` walks active agents until a short/empty page. Its page size
must be an integer 1..200 (larger sizes throw before HTTP); it does not silently stop
after 200 total agents. At the maximum offset it throws rather than truncate silently.
CLI: `nixflex agents list --status all --search Support --limit 50 --offset 50`.
Python (sync or await): `client.agents.list(status='all', search='Support', limit=50, offset=50)`.
MCP: `list_agents` takes the same four fields; no new tool or confirmation needed.

Database failures return `503 agent_store_unavailable`, not an empty successful list.

### Read automatic knowledge terms

Automatic knowledge terms are read-only. They come from valid, unsuppressed live pieces, keep source spelling, and are ranked by importance, essential identity, repeated support and stable tie-breaks. Generic terms are filtered. The default limit is 80 per agent; platform configuration can choose 0–100. Customer terms take priority and stay first on calls; duplicates and weaker automatic terms are removed to fit the call limits. The returned list is not a promise that every term will be sent on a call. Read [automatic keyterms](/api-reference/knowledge/get-agents-target-knowledge-keyterms). The optional `knowledge_keyterms` array appears when knowledge is enabled and filters against the saved customer terms.

summary: Get an agent in the authenticated account.
notes:
Fetch an owned agent using its `agent_id`.
Returns the same reviewed safe settings as create/update/list, including response delay,
STT controls, timezone, SMS settings, extraction, voicemail and retention.
No carrier auth token or unreviewed future column is returned.

GET still returns an owned soft-disabled agent; `is_active` is false.

| HTTP/code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Owned agent and its settings |
| 404 not_found | Missing or belongs to another account (same response) |
| 503 agent_store_unavailable | Storage could not be checked; do not interpret as missing |

### Read automatic knowledge terms

Automatic knowledge terms are read-only. They come from valid, unsuppressed live pieces, keep source spelling, and are ranked by importance, essential identity, repeated support and stable tie-breaks. Generic terms are filtered. The default limit is 80 per agent; platform configuration can choose 0–100. Customer terms take priority and stay first on calls; duplicates and weaker automatic terms are removed to fit the call limits. The returned list is not a promise that every term will be sent on a call. Read [automatic keyterms](/api-reference/knowledge/get-agents-target-knowledge-keyterms). The optional `knowledge_keyterms` array appears when knowledge is enabled and filters against the saved customer terms.

summary: Switch an owned agent off by setting is_active to false. GET still returns the inactive record. This is not permanent erasure.
notes:
This operation only writes `is_active=false` and updates the timestamp.
In plain words: **switch off**, not permanent deletion or a wait-for-live-calls operation.
It does not detach phone numbers, erase the row/history, or send carrier requests.

The existing response is kept for compatibility, but its wording means **soft disable**:



GET by ID can still return the owned disabled agent. List defaults to active only;
use `status=disabled` or `status=all` to include it.
PUT `{"is_active":true}` can re-enable it. This is not the dashboard's permanent erasure process.

The update must affect an owned row before success is returned.
Missing/foreign rows return `404 not_found`; database failures return
`503 agent_store_unavailable`. Check the agent before retrying an uncertain result.

summary: Owned public numbers only; pending imports and internal browser identities are hidden. Without limit/cursor the legacy envelope stays unchanged. count is returned rows, not total. Paged reads order by created_at DESC NULLS LAST, phone_number DESC; live traversal, not a snapshot.
notes:
Returns public numbers owned by your API key. Pending imports and internal
browser-test identities are hidden. Both API-added and dashboard-added numbers
are included. The dashboard Phone numbers page is unchanged.

### Query parameters

| Parameter | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `agent_id` | string | Optional exact agent filter |
| `provider` | `twilio` or `telnyx` | Optional exact carrier filter |
| `limit` | integer 1–100 | Opt into cursor paging |
| `cursor` | string | Opaque `next_cursor` from the previous page. With cursor alone limit defaults to 50 |

Without pagination parameters the existing `{ phone_numbers, count }` envelope
stays unchanged. The configured database row cap still applies; there is no
guaranteed 1,000-row contract. Use paging to traverse large accounts.
`count` ALWAYS means rows in this response, never the account total.



Paged responses add `next_cursor` (string or null) and `has_more` (boolean).
Keep the account and filters unchanged; pass the cursor unchanged and URL-encoded.
Invalid limit, provider or cursor returns `400 invalid_number_query`.



Numbers are newest first. Paged reads break equal timestamps by phone number
descending and put missing timestamps last. Follow `next_cursor` until null,
even if fewer than `limit` rows arrive. This is a live list, not a snapshot:
new imports appear on a fresh traversal; removed rows can disappear between pages.

Empty lists return 200 with count 0, not 404. The existing Twilio number SID stays
for compatibility. Credentials and internal row/account IDs never appear.
`source` is descriptive api/dashboard (null for unknown legacy origin),
not writable and never a permission. See [Get phone number](/api-reference/phone-numbers/get)
for full saved settings and [seven switches](/api-reference/phone-numbers/switches).

summary: Get a phone number in the authenticated account.
notes:
Use E.164 and URL-encode the leading plus: `/v1/phone-numbers/%2B12025550100`.
Requires an active API key/account. Unknown numbers, other accounts, pending imports
and internal browser-test numbers all return `404 number_not_found`.

The response is `{ "phone_number": { ... } }`. Every field below is present;
unset saved overrides remain null. This is not a dump of the database row.

| Fields | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `phone_number`, `agent_id`, `provider`, `created_at` | Public number, assigned public agent identifier, carrier and creation date |
| `source` | Read-only `api` / `dashboard`; null for unknown legacy origin. Descriptive, not a permission |
| `inbound_enabled`, `outbound_enabled`, `sms_reply_enabled` | Incoming calls, outbound call permission, automatic SMS replies |
| `web_agent_enabled`, `web_calls_enabled`, `web_functions_enabled`, `monitor_enabled` | Saved website and monitoring switches |
| `web_calls_effective` | Read-only website voice switch eligibility: saved voice ON and Web agent not OFF |
| `record_call`, `recording_source` | Saved recording override and source; null inherits agent |
| `custom_prompt`, `sms_prompt`, `web_prompt` | Separate call business profile, SMS instructions and website instructions |
| `voice_id`, `speaking_rate`, `dtmf_enabled`, `require_booking_confirmation` | Saved voice, speed, keypad and booking-confirmation overrides |
| `voicemail_leave_enabled`, `voicemail_message` | Saved per-number voicemail; dashboard-origin numbers use the agent policy instead |
| `telnyx_key_status` | Safe status below; no full key or full fingerprint |

Effective voice is only a switch calculation, not a guarantee that a call can start.
Account/agent activity, billing, authorization and existing admission checks still apply.
Legacy null Web agent values retain the existing engine's enabled interpretation.
No value is written by this request; it never changes the saved voice switch.

### Telnyx key status

Same projection as the dashboard:



`fingerprint` is at most 16 characters; the previous-key deadline is null when
absent/expired. `set` and `verified` describe stored key state, not provider health.
Twilio numbers normally have false/false/null/null key metadata.

To install or rotate a Telnyx signature key, send `telnyx_public_key` through the
existing import/PATCH candidate flow. A successful save is NOT verification.
Only the engine's valid signed-callback flow can verify a candidate; read back this
status after the normal callback test. There is no API field to force verified.
See [update](/api-reference/phone-numbers/update) and [import](/api-reference/phone-numbers/import).

Credentials, carrier account secrets, full signature keys, full fingerprints,
internal row/account/import IDs and operation tokens are never returned.

summary: Get number usage in the authenticated account.
notes:
Draft for API Area 1 Group 3. Requires its staging release. The kit changes below
are local/unpublished until separately released. This is a read-only request.

Use an active API key. Ownership comes only from that key, never a request field.
URL-encode the plus in E.164: `/v1/phone-numbers/%2B12025550123/usage`.
Absent, another owner's, pending and internal browser-test numbers return
`404 number_not_found`. Both API-imported and dashboard-imported owned numbers work.

### Period and time zone

- `period`: `today`, `7`, `14`, `30`, `90`, or `all` (default).
- `time_zone`: an IANA zone such as `Europe/London`, or `UTC` (default).
- Finite periods start at local midnight, including today: 7 means today plus
  six earlier calendar dates, not the previous 168 hours. DST is respected.
- `period_start` is inclusive; `null` for all retained history. `period_end` is
  the inclusive server query cutoff, not a future day-end. All returned ISO times
  identify absolute instants; an offset may differ from the selected zone.
- Use the dashboard browser's zone to compare. Requests at different instants
  can differ if new activity arrives, costs settle or retention removes history.
- Duplicate parameters, unknown parameters and invalid values return 400.

### Response and meaning

The envelope is `{ "usage": { ... } }`. It includes the number, period, zone,
boundaries and these fields:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `call_count` | Retained call rows in this period, including unpriced/zero-duration rows |
| `total_ms`, `minutes` | Sum of stored duration in milliseconds; minutes = total_ms / 60000, rounded to six decimals |
| `last_call` | Latest call creation timestamp in the period, or null |
| `total_cost`, `currency` | Exact decimal string of recorded call charges; currency USD |
| `unpriced_calls` | Number of calls with NULL cost; a known zero cost is not unpriced |
| `sms_sent`, `sms_received`, `sms_count` | Outbound, inbound and all retained SMS rows; counts are messages, not billable segments |
| `web_chats` | Distinct session IDs with messages in the period, scoped to the current number row |
| `unused` | Zero calls AND zero SMS. A number with only web chat is still “Unused” |
| `history_note` | Retained history, not a billing ledger; provider SMS charges are not included |

`duration_unit` is `milliseconds`; `start_inclusive` and `end_inclusive` are true.
For display, round minutes to at most two decimals and cost to two decimals, as
the dashboard does. Do not recompute cost from minutes or a current price.

Retention can reduce these totals. Calls and SMS are attributed by owner plus
business E.164 number (outbound = from; otherwise = to), exactly like the dashboard.
Same-owner re-import can therefore include that owner's older call/SMS history;
another owner's rows are excluded. Web chats additionally require the current
number-row generation; old/unbound generations are excluded. This is not lifetime
carrier usage, a payment statement, a ledger, or a guarantee that a call is settled.
No raw calls, messages, recordings, credentials or internal account IDs are returned.

### Query budget and failures

The aggregate has a three-second database RPC budget and a five-second engine
wait limit, with number/owner/time indexes. It returns full totals or
`503 usage_unavailable`, never a partial aggregate or false zero. Try a smaller
period or retry later; do not loop aggressively. The normal API rate limit applies.

### Client method examples



```javascript
const { usage } = await client.phoneNumbers.usage('+12025550123', {
  period: '30', time_zone: 'Europe/London'
});
console.log(usage.total_cost); // exact decimal USD string
```

```python
result = client.phone_numbers.usage('+12025550123', period='30', time_zone='Europe/London')
# Same method on AsyncNixflex: await client.phone_numbers.usage(...)
```

```shell
nixflex numbers usage +12025550123 --period 30 --time-zone Europe/London --json
```

The existing read-only MCP `list_phone_numbers` tool has an additive usage mode:

```json
{"phone_number":"+12025550123","usage":true,"period":"30","time_zone":"Europe/London"}
```

Do not combine usage with list filters/paging. Without `usage:true`, the existing
list/single-settings tool behaviour remains unchanged. No new credentials or
permissions are needed. Browser RPC grants have not been expanded.

usage.history_note: Usage reflects retained records for this number generation.

summary: Guarded cleanup request for an owned call. Can refuse with 409/503 for in-progress/unsettled work or pending/failed cleanup. Not a promise of immediate all-copy erasure. Never blindly retry an uncertain response.
notes:
Requests guarded cleanup of one owned call. It is not a promise of immediate erasure of every copy.

An ended, settled call with a skipped managed recording can now complete a narrow empty-recording path. It requires proof of no stored object or carrier copy, a closed upload fence, complete saved call context, finished post-call work and settlement, no active writers/read leases or unknown copies, and a fresh owned-resource absence check. Any missing or unknown proof keeps the strict 409 refusal. A stored object row in any state does not qualify. Bulk and account deletion are unchanged.

A recording marked unavailable (tracking_unavailable), an empty URL or zero recorded seconds is not proof of erasure. The call may have completed normally while deletion remains pending. The narrow path makes no carrier or storage DELETE request.

### Not reversible

<Warning>Completed removal cannot be undone through this API. Do not promise immediate completion, automatic retry or removal from customer-owned storage and external copies. Lost replies leave the outcome unknown: check before retrying.</Warning>

Billing and retained financial evidence are unaffected. Call usage remains part of the account's financial records. This operation does not promise to remove webhook delivery logs.
responseNotes:
The example shows successful narrow empty-recording cleanup: `deleted` is true and `recording_deleted` is false.

`recording_deleted` reflects whether the legacy cleanup path counted a requested recording or transfer-audio path. That path can request removal of a possible transfer-audio object even when none exists. The flag is not proof that a recording existed or every copy was erased. A refused or unknown request must not be shown as deleted.
errorNotes:
| Status | Code | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `not_found` | No call with that ID on your account. Also returned for a call you have already deleted. |
| 409 | `call_in_progress` | The call is still in progress; wait for it to end. |
| 409 | `deletion_unsettled` | Outcome/charge is not confirmed; do not claim deletion. |
| 409 | `recording_cleanup_pending`, `cleanup_pending_confirmation` | Storage/transfer-audio cleanup needs confirmation; contact support. |
| 409 | `deletion_cleanup_failed` | Cleanup did not finish; contact support before retrying. |
| 503 | `deletion_unavailable` | Safety could not be checked; deletion is not confirmed. |

Only calls made with your own API key can be deleted; another account's call ID returns the same `404`.

Safety refusals include `details.deleted=false`, `details.account_locked=false`, the `reason` code, nullable `review_due`, and `details.safe_to_retry=false`. A review timestamp is not a promise that cleanup will finish by that time. Keep the pending state and reconcile through support before another deliberate action.

summary: Guarded call cleanup request; does not delete SMS or close the account. Can refuse with 409/503 while work or cleanup confirmation is pending. Legacy recording counters are not all-copy erasure proof. Never blindly retry an uncertain response.
notes:
Requests guarded cleanup of owned call history. The current public guard can
hold nonempty cleanup for storage/transfer-audio confirmation. This is not an
immediate account-erasure workflow and does **not** delete SMS messages. The
separate reviewed safe-delete design remains pending; no safety fence is removed.

### Not reversible

<Warning>
  This is destructive if allowed. SDK changes never automatically retry it;
  a lost reply may follow partial progress. Check before retrying. There is no
  undo through this API; no promise about customer-owned or exported copies.
</Warning>

### What this does NOT do

- This call-data request does not delete your agents, phone numbers or API keys.
- Billing and invoices are unaffected. Past usage stays on your invoices; billing records are retained for tax purposes.
- Account deletion is a separate dashboard-owner workflow with pending states;
  this endpoint does not close an account or certify its complete erasure.
responseNotes:
Legacy  shape; an already-empty scope can return:



| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `calls_deleted` | number | Call records removed. |
| `recordings_deleted` | number | Legacy requested-storage-path count, including possible whisper paths; not proof of objects found or every copy erased. |
| `sms_deleted` | number | Compatibility field; this route does not delete SMS and returns zero. |

Refusals use 409 for in-progress, unsettled or pending/failed cleanup, and 503 when
safety cannot be checked. See [Delete call](/api-reference/calls/delete) for the
codes. A safety refusal includes `details.deleted=false` and
`details.safe_to_retry=false`; show the reason instead of “deleted”. No completion
deadline or all-copy erasure guarantee is made by this response.

summary: What your agent knows about one caller on one of your numbers - what you set and what the engine learned, in one record.
notes:
Returns what your agent knows about one caller on one of your numbers - what you set and what the engine has learned, in one record.

An owned business number with no caller record returns **404 caller_not_found**, with message `No caller record for CALLER on BUSINESS.` A number outside the account returns **404 phone_number_not_found**, with message `Phone number BUSINESS is not on this account.` Check the code as well as the status.
responseNotes: Only fields that have a value are returned. `last_call` and `open_item` are written by the engine after a call - `last_call` is what the caller **wanted**, never what happened.
errorNotes:
| Code | Cause |
|---|---|
| `phone_number_not_found` | The number is not on this account |
| `caller_not_found` | No record for that caller on that number |

context.name: Sam Carter
context.open_item: waiting for a callback about a refund

summary: Sets the details for one caller on one of your numbers. Creates the record if needed. A field left out keeps its value; send null to remove it. last_call and open_item are engine-only and are rejected.
notes:
Sets what your agent knows about one caller on one of your numbers. Creates the record if it does not exist.

See [Caller context](/concepts/caller-context) for how the agent uses these details on a call.

### Body parameters

Send at least one field. A field you leave out keeps its current value; send `null` to remove it.

| Field | Type | Max length | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string or null | 120 | Full name - first and last. The agent uses it naturally and confirms it before booking. |
| `email` | string or null | 120 | Must be a valid address. Confirmed with the caller before it is used for an action. |
| `phone` | string or null | 40 | A contact number other than the one they call from. |
| `location` | string or null | 120 | Free text - city, area, postal code, whatever suits your market. |
| `reference_id` | string or null | 64 | An account, order or booking reference the caller uses. |
| `preference` | string or null | 200 | A short preference, for example `prefers morning appointments`. |

`last_call` and `open_item` are written by the engine after each call and cannot be set here - sending them returns `engine_only_field`. An unrecognised field name is rejected rather than ignored, so a typo never disappears silently.

### Behaviour

- **Last write wins per field.** If the caller confirms a different email on a call, the engine stores the new one and the next call uses it. Send the field again to set it back.
- **An empty value never erases.** Only an explicit `null` removes a field.
- **One record per number, per caller.** The same person on another of your numbers is a separate record - import them to each number you want them recognised on.
- Takes effect on the caller's next call or text. Calls already in progress are unaffected.
responseNotes: `context` is the whole record - your fields together with anything the engine has learned.
errorNotes:
| Code | Cause |
|---|---|
| `phone_number_not_found` | The number is not on this account |
| `engine_only_field` | `last_call` or `open_item` was sent |
| `unknown_field` | A field name that is not in the table above |
| `invalid_email` | `email` is not a valid address |
| `field_too_long` | A value is over its maximum length |
| `missing_field` | No fields were sent |

summary: Connect Google Calendar to an owned Nixflex number. Create a consent link, handle return codes and keep OAuth credentials private.
notes:
Assign an agent first. A number can use one booking provider; a Cal.com connection conflicts with Google Calendar. Open the returned URL in the user's browser to obtain consent. The link expires after ten minutes and can be used once. A saved connection that needs reconnect can request fresh consent; reconnect preserves business settings.

Use HTTPS for `return_url`. Custom app schemes require the service operator to approve ownership and add the scheme for the organisation; there is no public allowlist endpoint. Do not use credentials, fragments, whitespace, backslashes or OAuth-secret query names. The app receives status only, never OAuth codes or tokens.

| Redirect result | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `status=connected&phone_number=...` | Connection saved for that number. |
| `status=error&code=access_denied` | Consent was refused. |
| `status=error&code=expired_link` | Link expired or the bound identity/revision changed. Start a new flow. |
| `status=error&code=already_connected` | Existing connection or a booking-provider conflict. Read current state. |
| `status=error&code=google_error` | Google connection could not complete. |

Ordinary return URL query parameters are kept; reserved `status`, `code`, and `phone_number` values are replaced. Expired, replayed or missing state without a trusted destination shows a local 400 error instead of redirecting. A revoked app scheme also uses a local error. Never accept a return destination from callback query parameters.
responseNotes: The URL is short-lived and private. Do not log or cache it.
errorNotes: A Member dashboard session cannot connect. Read status after a lost response before creating another consent link.

summary: Read the Google Calendar connection for an owned Nixflex number, including reconnect state and whether caller invitations are enabled.
notes: `connected: true` means a saved connection exists. If `needs_reconnect: true`, ask for fresh consent; do not label it ready for booking. Disconnected or absent connections return `connected: false`. GET checks Google access with a bounded refresh. A temporary provider failure returns 503 and must not be displayed as a disconnected account. No credential is returned.
responseNotes: `send_invites` is always a boolean; an absent saved value reads as true.
errorNotes: Treat 503 as an unknown check result. Do not overwrite the last known connection state.

summary: Disconnect Google Calendar from an owned Nixflex number. Remove local access and understand in-flight bookings and shared Google grants.
notes: Local access is removed for this number, including its older agent-wide calendar fallback. Other numbers keep their access. Remote Google revocation is best effort and can be skipped where grants may be shared. Already-loaded booking tools check the stored connection before a write; an operation already dispatched cannot be recalled.
responseNotes: A successful local disconnect returns exactly `ok: true, connected: false`.
errorNotes: Read status after a lost response before another deliberate disconnect.

summary: Set calendar timezone, weekly hours, slot length and caller invitations for an owned Nixflex number. Omitted settings retain their saved value.
notes:
Send one or more fields. Omission preserves each saved value. `hours` replaces the whole map: provide all seven lowercase weekday names, each null or exactly `["HH:MM", "HH:MM"]`. Closing must follow opening on the same day; overnight intervals are refused. Legacy defaults are Monday–Friday 09:00–17:00, 30-minute slots and `primary` calendar.

`send_invites` is a JSON boolean. Existing connections default to true when the value is absent. A string such as `"false"`, null or a number is refused. When enabled, Google is asked to email the caller an invitation, update or cancellation; Google controls delivery. No owner attendee or separate owner email is added. Setting false requests no Google notification. See [booking flow](/actions/booking-confirmation).
responseNotes: The response contains safe settings and `send_invites`; it contains no OAuth credentials.
errorNotes: `invalid_send_invites` means the value was not a boolean. PATCH requires a connected calendar.

summary: Update carrier credentials for an imported Nixflex phone number in place. Preserve settings and handle uncertain routing or credential saves safely.
notes:
Send exactly the credential pair for the number's existing carrier. Twilio uses `twilio_sid` and `twilio_token`; Telnyx uses `telnyx_api_key` and `telnyx_connection_id` for your existing TeXML app. Mixed pairs, extra fields, a provider switch, agent fields and settings fields are refused. Outer whitespace is trimmed; blank values are refused. Telnyx values cannot contain CR, LF or NUL. Secrets are write-only and are never returned.

Verification checks that the new carrier account owns this exact number before changing routing. Twilio voice, SMS and status URLs are repointed to Nixflex and application/trunk overrides are cleared. Telnyx attaches the submitted TeXML app without changing shared app webhooks. The number ID, assigned agent, prompts, switches, pickup delay, integrations and history remain.

A changed Telnyx credential identity clears verification evidence, keeps the public key and needs the existing fresh test-call and approval flow. Identical current credentials retain existing verification when the resource also matches. Do not delete and re-import a number to recover from an uncertain credential update.
responseNotes: The response confirms the owned number and carrier. No credential or resource snapshot is returned.
errorNotes: `invalid_credentials` is HTTP 400, not an API-authentication 401. `carrier_outcome_unknown`: stop automatic retries and contact support with `details.operation_id` if present. `credential_save_pending`: the carrier change is confirmed; deliberately resubmit identical details to finish the local save without a second carrier change. A pending number/release operation must be resolved first. Never use delete/re-import as recovery.
